name: Kenvue

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Kenvue Logo Black RGB.svg)

description: Kenvue sells household-name consumer health brands (Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine, Band-Aid, Aveeno, Johnson's) that it inherited from Johnson & Johnson. Retailers, pharmacies and distributors buy the products, and it also sells online; revenue comes from unit sales of branded over-the-counter medicines, skin and hair care, oral care, baby care and wound care. About 60 percent of sales volume is made in its own plants and the rest by contract manufacturers. It is being acquired by Kimberly-Clark for stock plus cash, expected to close in Q4 2026.

employees.note: Approximately 22,000 employees; about 23 percent North America, 28 percent EMEA, 30 percent APAC, 19 percent Latin America.

businessLines.name: Self Care
businessLines.how: Retailers and pharmacies buy branded over-the-counter medicines (cough, cold, allergy, pain, digestive, smoking cessation) by the case; revenue per unit sold and partly seasonal (cold and flu); some products such as Tylenol and Zyrtec are made by third parties.

businessLines.name: Skin Health and Beauty
businessLines.how: Retailers buy face, body, hair and sun-care products; repeat consumer purchases of premium-priced dermatologist-recommended brands, supported by heavy advertising spend.

businessLines.name: Essential Health
businessLines.how: Retailers buy oral care, baby care, wound care and feminine care products by the case; staple purchases with steadier demand.

brands.name: Tylenol
brands.note: Self Care; subject to Texas Attorney General suit (Oct 2025) alleging an acetaminophen link to autism and ADHD

whatsNext.text: Acquisition by Kimberly-Clark: each Kenvue share receives 0.14625 K-C shares plus $3.50 cash; Kenvue holders would own about 46 percent of the combined company. Shareholder votes passed 2026-01-29; foreign regulatory approvals outstanding.
